cells.source_title: World Bank, The Little Data Book on Financial Inclusion 2025 (Global Findex Database 2025), Egypt, Arab Rep. country page (p. 56): Mobile money account (% age 15+) = 15.6
cells.search_trail: 2026-08-22: (1) World Bank API, Global Findex database (source 28) — restructured 2025 databank no longer exposes a headline 'Mobile money account (% age 15+)' series under an obvious code (checked all 241 indicator stems; only sub-indicators like fin16 'Ever had a mobile money account' remain); (2) Little Data Book on Financial Inclusion 2025 PDF downloaded and Egypt page (p. 56) read directly — 15.6 (2024 survey, Findex 2025 wave); (3) Egypt Findex 2025 microdata catalog entry (7897) confirms the 2024 Egypt survey exists. Stopped at T1.
cells.notes: Confirms the prior desk-pass value of 15.6 but replaces its inadmissible source ('FinStatGlobe compilation', T5) with the T1 original. Observation year is 2024 (Findex 2025 wave fieldwork). Prior's claim of 'up from 2.9% in 2021' was not re-verified in this pass. SINGLE-SOURCE FLAG: Findex is the only survey measuring this construct; the second link is the same survey's microdata catalog, not an independent confirmation (CBE publishes registered mobile-wallet counts, a different metric). Threshold context (H 10/25/50/75): 15.6 sits between the 10 and 25 marks — level assignment left to scoring.
cells.protocol_issues: Machine-fetch breakage: the 2025 restructure of the Findex databank (source 28) removed/renamed the headline mobile money account code, so the 'API/T1 first' route fails for this row; the PDF Little Data Book is the practical resolvable T1 artefact. Also: triangulation rule 2 cannot be satisfied for any Findex-only construct — permanent single-source condition worth acknowledging in the protocol.

cells.source_title: World Bank Global Findex Database 2025, Egypt: Own a mobile phone, men (con1.2) = 91.7% vs women (con1.1) = 77.3%, age 15+, 2024 — gap 14.4 percentage points (derived by subtraction of the two published series)
cells.search_trail: 2026-08-22: (1) World Bank API Findex source 28, EGY con1/con1.1/con1.2 — 2024 values 84.56 / 77.28 / 91.67; cross-checked against Little Data Book 2025 Egypt page ('Has a personal mobile phone' all adults 84.6, women 77.3). (2) GSMA Mobile Gender Gap Report 2025 (2024 survey; canonical page gsma.com/gender-gap-2025, PDF retrieved via PTA-hosted copy) Figure 2: Egypt mobile ownership men 89%, women 86%, gender gap 3%. T1 found first and recorded per tier order; GSMA retained as documented conflicting T4.
cells.notes: DIVERGES FROM PRIOR: prior recorded -2 pp from GSMA MGGR 2023 (2022 survey data, women slightly ahead of men). Two things changed: (a) fresher data exist (both Findex and GSMA surveyed Egypt in 2024); (b) the two 2024 surveys conflict sharply — Findex implies a 14.4 pp male advantage in mobile ownership, GSMA 2025 implies ~3 pp (89 vs 86). Recorded value follows tier order (Findex T1). CONFLICT FLAG: with threshold L 20/10/5/2, the band conclusion flips materially between sources (14.4 pp vs 3 pp); do not treat this row as settled. The 14.4 value is arithmetic (91.67 - 77.28) on two published series of the same survey, disclosed as derived, not itself a published number.
cells.protocol_issues: (1) Indicator is defined in percentage points, but GSMA's headline metric is a relative gap ((M-W)/M) — unit ambiguity invites silent apples-to-oranges comparisons across passes (prior's -2 was GSMA's relative metric). (2) Same-vintage T1 vs T4 sources conflict far beyond sampling noise (14.4 pp vs 3 pp, both 2024 fieldwork); protocol has no adjudication step beyond 'T1 wins' — flag for Katreyna. (3) The scored value requires subtracting two published series; protocol is silent on whether derived-by-arithmetic values count as 'a number named by the source'.

cells.value: DATA GAP — searched (2026-08-22, in order): Global Findex 2025 databank/API (no farmer-level digital-services indicator); web search for FAO / World Bank national estimates of Egyptian farmers using digital agricultural services (none names a national share); IFPRI Egypt SSP publications — Working Paper 43 (Sept 2024) and IFPRI DP 2359 (2025) provide two-governorate survey data only (Minya + Beni Suef, n=3,332); ICARDA 'Current Situation of Digital Agriculture in Egypt' (CGSpace hdl 10568/138425, limited access — abstract carries no reach numbers); CGIAR/IFPRI CSA policy note Dec 2025 (platform descriptions, no reach share). No national estimate with real provenance exists.
cells.source_title: Closest evidence (regional, not national): Abdelaziz & Tarek, 'Digital Tools for Smallholders in Egypt: The Launch of a New Price Monitoring Tool - Mahsoly', IFPRI Egypt SSP Working Paper 43, Sept 2024
cells.search_trail: 2026-08-22: Findex databank source 28 (no indicator) -> FAO/World Bank web search for national estimates (none) -> IFPRI Egypt SSP WP43 + DP2359 (regional survey: at baseline only 20% of sampled Minya/Beni Suef farmers had heard of Mahsoly; 54% cite unawareness of digital apps as adoption barrier; 97% own a mobile phone, 72% a smartphone) -> ICARDA digital-ag review (limited access) -> CGIAR CSA policy note Dec 2025. Gap recorded.
cells.notes: REFUTES the prior desk pass, which recorded a 'composite from platform user counts vs ~4M ag holdings (2020 census)' and assessed level 3 — that is a constructed estimate: no source names a national share, so under rule 1 it cannot stand as a value. Honest fragments for the narrative register: individual platform self-reports (Mahsoly, AlMorshed Poultry '100,000+ users' each per the ICARDA 2025 review cited by the prior — not independently verifiable here, report is limited-access) against roughly 4M agricultural holdings would imply single-digit percentages, but composing that number would fabricate precision. This is exactly the kind of cell where an honest gap is the finding.
cells.protocol_issues: Indicator has no measurement infrastructure in Egypt: no national survey instrument (CAPMAS agricultural census, Findex, LSMS-type) captures farmer-level use of digital agricultural services. Platform self-reported user counts are T5-adjacent (vendor claims routed through a T2 review) and lack denominators, de-duplication, and active-use definitions. Recommend the ledger route this to a planned-measurement flag rather than periodic re-search.

cells.value: No quantified share published; qualitative evidence indicates local-language delivery of flagship services is effectively universal. All major identified digital-agriculture services in Egypt are delivered in Arabic: Hudhud (MALR/MCIT AI extension assistant — Arabic text/voice chat), El Mufeed (FAO/MALR advisory app, Arabic, built with farmer/rural-women input), Bashaer (CCIC-EMA climate recommendations), Nabta (IDSC awareness app), Mahsoly (price/marketing). No census of services with a language attribute exists from which a % could be computed.
cells.source_title: UN Egypt / FAO-MALR: 'FAO & MALR invite extension agents to use El Mufeed app and disseminate among targeted groups' (official programme page; El Mufeed is Arabic-language); corroborated by IFPRI Egypt CSA policy note (Dec 2025) naming Bashaer and Nabta
cells.search_trail: 2026-08-22: searched for any quantified language-coverage share (none exists); FAO Egypt / UN Egypt El Mufeed programme pages (Arabic app); SIS/MCIT reporting on Hudhud (Arabic AI chat app, text and voice); IFPRI Egypt Agriculture Apps Repository (egyptssp.ifpri.info/agricultural-apps/ — JS-rendered, not machine-readable in this pass); IFPRI CSA policy note Dec 2025 (Bashaer, Nabta). Recorded as citation, not number.
cells.notes: Consistent with prior ('High — most major platforms are Arabic'); this pass adds Bashaer and Nabta and pins resolvable sources. Not converted to '100%' — that would invent precision the sources do not carry (rule 7). Relevant nuance the % framing misses: Hudhud's voice interface matters more for the ~20% of farmers with no formal education than Arabic text per se (IFPRI WP43 baseline: 35% of sampled farmers report no formal education).
cells.protocol_issues: The protocol question posed by this cell: when a qualitative universal ('all major services are in Arabic') is well documented but no denominator exists, is the cell Measured, Documented, or Judged? Recorded here as Documented/citation. Deeper indicator-design defect: in a monolingual-majority country the indicator saturates trivially and discriminates nothing; if redefined as 'services available in each farmer's first language' (Nubian, Siwi Amazigh, Beja communities — no coverage found) or as 'literacy-appropriate delivery (voice/IVR)', the answer changes materially. Flag for the defect log.

cells.value: Rung facts. PRESENCE: one completed, published, independent impact evaluation of a digital-agriculture intervention in Egypt — Abdelaziz, F. & Abay, K.A., 'Digital literacy training to promote diffusion of digital agricultural tools to smallholder farmers: Evidence from a randomized intervention in Egypt', IFPRI Discussion Paper 2359 (Sept 2025); peer-reviewed in Food Policy (2026), doi:10.1016/j.foodpol.2026.103108. RCT in Minya & Beni Suef (baseline phone survey Jul-Sep 2023, n=3,332 farmers; four arms). Effects: uptake of digital tools +20 pp, utilization +26 pp, trust +8-13 pp. YIELD/INCOME RUNG: no independent in-country evidence isolating yield or income effects of digital-ag services was located — the RCT measured adoption/utilization/trust, not yield or income.
cells.source_title: Abdelaziz & Abay (2025/2026), IFPRI DP 2359 / Food Policy — RCT of digital literacy training for smallholder digital-tool adoption, Egypt
cells.search_trail: 2026-08-22: search for Egypt digital-ag RCTs/evaluations -> Abdelaziz & Abay located (CGSpace item + Food Policy DOI + AEA RCT Registry #12723 + IFPRI Egypt SSP announcement); second search for yield/income evaluations of El Mufeed / Mozare3 / Hudhud (none found — only platform descriptions and a global meta-analysis not specific to Egypt); IFPRI WP43 (Sept 2024) documents the same project's Mahsoly rollout (awareness 20%->80% post-training, downloads 10%->38%) — same intervention family, not an independent second evaluation.
cells.quality_evidence: Peer-reviewed publication (Food Policy, 2026); institutional anchoring in the IFPRI Egypt Strategy Support Program (CGIAR); pre-registered (AEA RCT Registry #12723, socialscienceregistry.org/trials/12723); ToT delivery model with MALR-adjacent local trainers — i.e., evidence generation is institutionalized within an ongoing country program, not a one-off donor study.
cells.scale_evidence: Single intervention study, two governorates (Minya, Beni Suef), n=3,332 at baseline; outcomes limited to adoption, utilization and trust. No yield/income estimates. Adjacent but non-qualifying: WFP Egypt reports ~20% household income increases on consolidated plots with climate-smart technologies (program self-report, not an independent digital-ag evaluation; cited in IFPRI CSA policy note Dec 2025).
cells.notes: CONFIRMS the prior desk pass ('utilization gains documented, yield gains not isolated') and upgrades it with the exact citation, DOI, sample and effect sizes. Rung reasoning: 'Adopted' because at least one completed independent evaluation exists and is published, but the indicator's named construct (yield/income evidence) is not yet documented and the evidence base is a single study — 'Operating' would overstate. The task brief's Nigeria reference (ABP evaluations) is not applicable to this Egypt bundle.
cells.protocol_issues: Ladder-rung semantics are undefined for evidence-type indicators: Absent/Announced/Adopted/Operating map awkwardly onto 'impact evidence exists'. Proposed mapping used here — Absent: no independent evaluations; Announced: registered/underway; Adopted: >=1 completed independent evaluation of a digital-ag intervention in-country; Operating: recurring evidence pipeline including yield/income outcomes. Needs a spec ruling so passes stay comparable.

cells.value: DATA GAP — searched (2026-08-22, in order): web search for EMA / CCIC / DAIRS advisory-reach statistics (none published); IFPRI Egypt CSA policy note Dec 2025 (CCIC issues daily climate warnings; CCIC-EMA 'Bashaer' platform delivers tailored climate-smart recommendations to farmers — no reach figures; FAO RNE panelist states 'communication gaps mean that many smallholders never receive' warnings); targeted search for Bashaer user/reach numbers (none); ICARDA digital-ag review abstract (DAIRS 'under development', no reach); FAO/WFP Egypt climate publications (project-level reach only, no national %). No percentage of Egyptian farmers receiving actionable climate advisories exists with provenance.
cells.source_title: Closest evidence: Hassan, G. & Tarek, A., 'Climate-smart agriculture and development practices in Egypt: Report on a policy seminar event', IFPRI Egypt policy note, Dec 2025 (Cairo BEP seminar, 25 May 2025)
cells.search_trail: 2026-08-22: EMA/CCIC/DAIRS reach search -> none; IFPRI CSA policy note (Bashaer + daily CCIC warnings, qualitative only) -> Bashaer-specific search -> none; ICARDA review abstract -> DAIRS under development; FAO SCALA Egypt page and WFP Egypt climate resilience publications -> program reach only. Gap recorded.
cells.notes: CONFIRMS the prior desk pass (no reach statistics found; DAIRS under development) and adds new presence facts postdating it: the CCIC (MALR Climate Change Information Center, dir. Mohamed Fahim) now issues daily climate warnings, and the CCIC-EMA Bashaer platform is operating as a delivery channel — so the delivery infrastructure exists, but its reach is unmeasured. FAO RNE's 2025 statement that many smallholders never receive warnings indicates reach is well below universal without quantifying it. With threshold H 20/40/60/80 unmeasurable, this stays a gap, not a low score.
cells.protocol_issues: Reach ('% farmers receiving actionable advisories') is unmeasured by any Egyptian institution; what exists is supply-side presence (warnings issued, platforms live). The indicator conflates advisory production with farmer receipt — the FAO RNE 'two gaps' framing (warnings lack actionable advice; many never receive them) is precisely the measurement hole. Ledger should route to planned measurement (e.g., a module in any forthcoming DAIRS/Bashaer M&E or IFPRI follow-up survey) rather than re-search.

bundle_issues: Four issues affect bundle G as a whole. (1) Findex databank restructure: the 2025 wave's databank (World Bank API source 28) dropped/renamed headline series (mobile money account % adults has no obvious code among the 241 stems), so any 'machine-fetchable T1' rows pointing at old Findex codes will silently fail — the Little Data Book 2025 PDF and microdata catalog are the reliable resolvable artefacts this cycle. (2) Source-conflict on gender gap (8.6): two reputable 2024-fieldwork surveys give irreconcilable values (Findex 14.4 pp vs GSMA MGGR 2025 ~3 pp / 3% relative); tier order dictates the T1 record, but the O1 band conclusion flips with source choice — this needs an adjudication note in the spec, and the prior's -2 pp (GSMA 2022 data, relative metric) should not be compared against pp values from Findex. (3) Egypt has no national measurement infrastructure for the farmer-facing outcome indicators (8.9 smallholder reach, 8.17 climate advisory reach): best available evidence is a two-governorate IFPRI survey program and platform self-reports without denominators; both cells are honest gaps and should be flagged for planned measurement, not periodic re-search. (4) Prior desk pass quality: exactly the load-bearing O1 numbers rested on inadmissible or constructed sources — 8.4 cited a T5 compilation site (value survived T1 verification), 8.9 was a composite the assessor built (refuted as a value). This pattern — weakest provenance on the outcomes pillar that headlines the diagnostic — is the failure mode the Source-Tier Protocol exists to catch.
